title: Nine Parts Manner
subtitle: 上司与领导 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 上司与领导（社会服务与人际沟通·职业与工作）
meta: 主题语境：上司与领导（社会服务与人际沟通·职业与工作）　|　核心词汇：boss　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 boss 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my mother was sent to answer ① a boss she could not please, and she said the pleasing was the whole of the lesson. The ② boss, meaning the man and not the office, was fifty years old and was obeyed by whoever came last; a boss, she said, is the only thing in a firm that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ boss in that office had the same manner, and the ④ boss at the end, meaning the one the clerk feared and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever listened to properly. A boss, my grandmother said, is nine parts manner and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the manner is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ boss was the whole of the office, meaning the authority it carried and not the man. The ⑥ boss, meaning the authority and not any of that, is the only thing in a firm that everybody answers and nobody questions; a boss, he said, is either someone you please or the only word that means both a man and an authority. She said the authority is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ boss had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the manner. The ⑧ boss of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was fifty years of manner and eleven years of answering; a boss, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ boss I remember is the one at the end, which was drawn in 1976 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ boss, my grandmother said in 1985, is the only thing that improves by being listened to; every boss, she said, is an authority that has agreed to look like a man. She said the authority was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 上司（指那个人本身，与职位相对）
C. 固定搭配：answer a boss 回答上司、向上司回话
D. n. 上司（指办公室里每一位）
E. n. 上司（指尽头那一位）
F. n. 上司（抽象：它所代表的权威）
G. n. 那份权威（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a boss she could not please
The boss, meaning the man and not the office
boss was the whole of the office
the boss had become a photograph in a report
The boss of the whole thing
A boss, my grandmother said in 1985

answers.why: answer a boss 意为“回答上司、向上司回话”，1955 年母亲被派去回一位她讨好不了的上司的话。
boss 意为“上司”，指那个人本身而不是职位，五十岁，由最后走的人服从。
boss 指办公室里每一位上司，每一位都是同样的做派。
boss 指尽头那一位（办事员害怕的那一位），是唯一有人认真听他说话的。
boss 意为“上司”，抽象指它所代表的权威，父亲说 boss 就是那间办公室的全部。
boss 为抽象用法，指那份权威本身，是公司里人人都回话、却没人质疑的东西。
boss 意为“老板、上司”，到 1971 年这位 boss 成了报告里的一张照片。
boss 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是五十年的做派和十一年的回话。
boss 意为“上司”，我记得的是尽头那一位，1976 年被画下来，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
boss 为抽象总称，祖母说上司是唯一会因为有人肯听他说话而变好的。
